hints.title: Categorizing Primary Assignments
hints.text: An employee has a primary department either if marked with primary_flag = "Y" or if they belong to only one department overall.

hints.title: Extracting Single-Department Workers
hints.text: Query employees having a count of one across their department affiliations.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT employee_id, department_id
FROM Employee
WHERE primary_flag = 'Y'
UNION
SELECT employee_id, department_id
FROM Employee
GROUP BY employee_id
HAVING COUNT(*) = 1;
```

complexity.time: O(N) pass for flagged rows + O(N) grouped scan with UNION deduplication
complexity.space: O(E) working memory for unique employee departments
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Complex subqueries in WHERE clauses can cause correlated full scans per row.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: UNION automatically handles cases where an employee with one department also has primary_flag = "Y".
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle both explicitly flagged primary departments and single-department defaults.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def find_primary_department(employee: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    flagged = employee[employee["primary_flag"] == "Y"][["employee_id", "department_id"]]
    counts = employee.groupby("employee_id")["department_id"].count().reset_index()
    single_emp_ids = counts[counts["department_id"] == 1]["employee_id"]
    single = employee[employee["employee_id"].isin(single_emp_ids)][["employee_id", "department_id"]]
    return pd.concat([flagged, single]).drop_duplicates()
solutions.approach: Union of flagged and single-department sets in pandas
